title: United States and United Kingdom strike Houthi targets in Yemen
body:
On the night of 11 to 12 January 2024 the United States and United Kingdom launched strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen. US President Joe Biden said they were a response to what he called "unprecedented" Houthi drone and missile attacks on commercial ships in the Red Sea. The US said Australia, Bahrain, Canada and the Netherlands supported the operation.

US Lt. Gen. Douglas Sims said nearly 30 locations were struck with more than 150 munitions. Houthi-run Al Masirah television reported that sites included the al-Dailami air base north of Sanaa, Hodeidah airport, a camp east of Saada, Taiz airport and an airport near Hajjah. The Houthis said five people were killed. Sims said he did not expect high casualties because many targets were in rural areas.

British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak called the strikes "necessary and proportionate." Biden said he would not hesitate to take further action if needed, and White House spokesperson John Kirby said the US was not seeking war with Yemen. The Houthi Supreme Political Council declared all American and British interests "legitimate targets," Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the attack would not go unanswered, and negotiator Mohammed Abdul-Salam said targeting of Israeli-linked ships would continue. Iran condemned the strikes, and Russia requested an urgent UN Security Council meeting. Yemen's Saudi-backed government blamed the Houthis for the strikes.
